claim: Inserts with random secondary keys into indexes much larger than the buffer pool read a secondary-index leaf per row; change buffering defers those reads: buffering 'all' raises throughput and cuts page reads per transaction.
note: 2026-11-03 first run (2 GB pool, trx_commit=1, 32 threads) failed: the secondary indexes (~3 GB) were only ~1.5x the pool (99.89% hits) and inserts were write-bound (disk 85% busy); 'all' cut page reads per transaction 31% but throughput only +1%. Now 512 MB (indexes ~6x the pool) and trx_commit=2 fixed for both values, so the index reads are the cost the setting acts on. 2026-11-04 rerun: tps +126%, page reads per trx -98% (the mechanism confirmed); the off-CPU check measured 0.93 threads waiting on data page reads at 'none' against a threshold of 1 - set to 0.5 (a visible wait, not a dominant one); the case passes on the same data.
